lines: Australia has committed to 82 percent renewable electricity by 2030.
In 2005, about 9 percent of Australia's electricity was renewable. Coal and gas made the rest.
The share stalled while the target was under review.
After the 2015 reset, it grew about 2.5 points a year, reaching 35 percent in 2024.
Fossil generation fell from 208 to 182 terawatt hours.
Solar and wind took over. They made 4.7 percent of renewable electricity in 2005, and 81.3 percent in 2024.
Wind overtook hydro in 2019. Solar overtook both a year later.
New Zealand runs at 85.5 percent renewable, and Germany at 54.5.
Australia, at 35, is just ahead of China at 33.7.
On a linear trend, the share reaches 37.8 percent by 2030, less than half the 82 percent target.
Australia is moving in the right direction, but not fast enough.
